pathway.title: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia — Outpatient Screening, Diagnosis and Surveillance
pathway.scope: Outpatient prenatal care. Risk assessment and aspirin prophylaxis from the first prenatal visit; blood pressure surveillance; diagnosis and severity classification after 20 weeks; outpatient expectant management. Ends at the trigger for admission or delivery.
pathway.target_population: Pregnant patients receiving prenatal care. The prophylaxis arm applies to all; diagnostic and surveillance arms apply after 20 0/7 weeks.

properties.title: Does this patient qualify for low-dose aspirin prophylaxis?
properties.prompt: Does this patient qualify for low-dose aspirin prophylaxis? Qualifies with ANY ONE high-risk factor (prior preeclampsia, multifetal gestation, chronic hypertension, pregestational type 1 or 2 diabetes, kidney disease, autoimmune disease such as SLE or antiphospholipid syndrome); OR TWO OR MORE moderate-risk factors (nulliparity, BMI >30, family history of preeclampsia in mother or sister, Black race, lower income, age 35 or older, personal history factors, in vitro conception); OR, on its own, Black race or lower income.

properties.title: Latest blood pressure at or above 140/90?
Has hypertension been confirmed per ACOG criteria?
properties.prompt: Is hypertension confirmed? Two readings with systolic 140 or above, or diastolic 90 or above, taken at least 4 hours apart, after 20 0/7 weeks, in a patient previously normotensive. Severe-range readings (160/110 or above) may be confirmed over minutes rather than hours.

properties.title: Diagnosis of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia established?
Diagnosis of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia established? (postpartum BP follow-up)
Diagnosis of gestational hypertension or preeclampsia established? (long-term CV risk counselling)
Does any objective finding preclude continued outpatient management?
Any severe feature on clinical assessment?
properties.prompt: Does the patient have ANY of the following? New-onset headache unresponsive to acetaminophen and not otherwise explained; visual disturbance; severe persistent right upper quadrant or epigastric pain unresponsive to analgesia; pulmonary oedema; transaminases more than twice the upper limit of normal; a doubling of serum creatinine; or severe-range blood pressure not responding to antihypertensive therapy.

properties.title: Is outpatient expectant management appropriate?
properties.prompt: Is outpatient expectant management appropriate? Requires no severe features, AND that the patient can adhere to weekly in-clinic visits, weekly laboratory testing, and fetal testing one to two times per week. Inability to adhere to this monitoring is itself an indication for admission.

properties.name: Aspirin 81 mg
properties.instructions: Guideline-sourced regimen, not label-sourced. MUST be exempted from any generic 'no NSAIDs after 20 weeks' rule — FDA names low-dose aspirin as the explicit exception.

properties.name: Labetalol
properties.instructions: CO-EQUAL FIRST LINE with nifedipine — ordering is presentational, not a ranking. Avoid in asthma, pre-existing myocardial disease, decompensated cardiac function, heart block, bradycardia. Neonatal hypotension, bradycardia, hypoglycaemia and respiratory depression reported after exposure near delivery.
properties.dose: 200 mg every 12 hours, up to 800 mg every 8-12 hours (max 2,400 mg/day); acute: 10-20 mg IV then 20-80 mg every 10-30 min, max 300 mg cumulative

properties.name: Nifedipine, extended release
properties.instructions: CO-EQUAL FIRST LINE with labetalol. Avoid in tachycardia. Never sublingual. PB 222 gives no extended-release regimen; dosing is from PB 203 and the FDA label.
properties.dose: 30-60 mg once daily, titrated over 7-14 days (max 120 mg/day)

properties.name: Nifedipine, immediate release
properties.instructions: IMMEDIATE RELEASE ONLY — urgent control agent, onset 5-10 minutes. These numbers must never be used for maintenance. Separate lane is deliberate: substituting extended release here would collide with labetalol's lane.
properties.dose: 10-20 mg orally, repeat after 20 min if needed, then 10-20 mg every 2-6 hours (max 180 mg/day)

properties.name: Methyldopa
properties.instructions: Contraindicated in active hepatic disease and with MAO inhibitors. PB 222 does not mention methyldopa at all; sourced from PB 203 and the FDA label.
properties.dose: 250 mg two or three times daily (max 3,000 mg/day)

properties.name: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, renin inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
properties.instructions: FDA BOXED WARNING at class level: these reduce fetal renal function and increase fetal and neonatal morbidity and death. Resulting oligohydramnios can cause pulmonary hypoplasia and skeletal deformation. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.

properties.name: Fetal biophysical profile with non-stress testing

properties.instructions: Review the urgent maternal warning signs (CDC Hear Her / AIM) with the patient and give her the handout; she should seek care immediately for any of them. The warning signs apply during pregnancy and for a year after birth. Source: https://www.cdc.gov/hearher/maternal-warning-signs/index.html

properties.topic: Measuring your blood pressure at home
properties.instructions: Use an upper-arm cuff, correctly sized — the cuff should be about one and a half times around your upper arm. Sit upright and rest for at least ten minutes first. Avoid tobacco and caffeine for thirty minutes beforehand. Home readings supplement your weekly in-clinic visit; they do not replace it. Validated upper-arm devices for pregnancy are listed by STRIDE BP; no wrist or finger device is validated for this use.

properties.topic: What we are not recommending, and why
properties.instructions: Bed rest is not recommended — the evidence does not support it. Salt restriction is not recommended. Routine calcium supplementation is not recommended in the United States, where baseline dietary calcium is adequate. Vitamins C and E, fish oil, garlic and vitamin D have no demonstrated benefit for prevention. After delivery, anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen are preferred over opioids — patients are often incorrectly told to avoid them.

properties.topic: Your heart health after this pregnancy
properties.instructions: A hypertensive disorder of pregnancy roughly doubles your later risk of cardiovascular disease, and the risk is higher after severe, recurrent or early-onset disease. This applies to gestational hypertension as well as preeclampsia. Tell every future clinician — especially your primary care provider — that you had this condition; there is no reliable diagnosis code that carries it forward for you. Healthy weight, exercise, diet and stopping smoking are the levers. In a future pregnancy this history alone qualifies you for aspirin prophylaxis.
Tell the patient and her family that a seizure is an emergency: call 911 right away. Source: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222.

properties.name: Postpartum blood pressure follow-up scheduled
properties.measure: Of patients with a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, the proportion with a postpartum blood pressure and symptom check SCHEDULED to occur within 3 days of discharge where persistent severe hypertension occurred during the birth admission, or within 7 days otherwise. Steward: AIM/ACOG (SHTN P2A/P2B). Measures scheduling, not attendance.

properties.name: Aspirin prophylaxis among eligible patients
properties.measure: Of patients with a documented qualifying risk profile, the proportion started on low-dose aspirin before 16 0/7 weeks of gestation. Steward: local — no national measure exists.

properties.interval: 12 0/7 to 28 0/7 weeks, optimally before 16 0/7; then daily until delivery
properties.description: Aspirin initiation window and duration.

properties.interval: At least once weekly, in clinic
properties.description: Blood pressure and symptom assessment plus weekly platelets, creatinine and liver enzymes. Repeat sooner if progression is a concern.

properties.interval: Growth ultrasound every 3-4 weeks; amniotic fluid at least weekly; antenatal test 1-2 times weekly
properties.description: Fetal surveillance during expectant management.

properties.interval: Within 3 days of discharge if severe hypertension occurred, otherwise within 7 days
properties.description: Postpartum blood pressure and symptom check with escalation instructions. ACOG's outer bound is 7-10 days, and 72 hours for severe hypertension.
